methods.label: Use the sine-cosine identity
methods.explanation:
The relation \(\sin x=3\cos x\) lets us write both the identity and the desired product using \(\cos^2x\). Substituting into \(\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1\) gives
\[
9\cos^2x+\cos^2x=1,
\qquad \cos^2x=\frac1{10}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\sin x\cos x=3\cos^2x=\frac3{10}.
\]
No sign choice is needed, so this works for every angle satisfying the condition. The answer is \(\frac3{10}\), choice E.
methods.levelReason: A basic same-angle trigonometric identity and substitution suffice, within AMC 12 scope.
